From the makers of EditBase

More apps from KTEC

EditBase has five companions in the Nextcloud App Store. Each does a single job inside Nextcloud, keeps its data on your own server, and is free software. Each has a page of its own here.

AppWhat it is forWho uses it
RegiBaseA personal database with fields you designEveryone
FormulaBaseA calculator for your everyday formulasEveryone
NetBaseThe devices on your network, and tools for themAdministrators and chosen groups
Talk-BotAI chat in Nextcloud TalkWhoever the administrator allows
AI-HubOne AI gateway for every app on the serverSet up by administrators

Working together

The apps know about each other. EditBase brings in records from RegiBase and formulas from FormulaBase, already laid out, and its AI assistant can read from both when the administrator allows it. AI-Hub is the common AI interface of the series: EditBase already asks it, and the other apps are being moved onto it in turn, so the AI service, its key and its limits are set once. Each app is installed on its own and needs none of the others. They all follow your Nextcloud: its users and groups, its sharing, its language and its theme.

Installing them

  1. Sign in to Nextcloud as an administrator and open Apps.
  2. Search for RegiBase, FormulaBase, NetBase, Talk-Bot or AI-Hub.
  3. Press Download and enable.

Free software

All six apps are AGPL. Their source is on GitHub under ktec-nc-apps, where problems and ideas are welcome.

RegiBase — a personal database

RegiBase keeps the information you want to have to hand: credit cards, bank accounts, online accounts, memberships, licences, contacts and anything else. Start from a template or design the fields yourself, each with its own rules for what may be typed in it, then browse the records as a list, a spreadsheet-like table or cards.

Secret fields, such as passwords, PINs and card numbers, can be encrypted in the browser with AES-GCM: the server never sees the master key or the words. Forget the master key, and nobody can read those fields again.

Three layers guard against losing anything:

  1. Snapshots: every change and deletion is kept, and Ctrl+Z takes back the last one.
  2. Versions by session: everything done until the browser is closed can be undone at once.
  3. An encrypted backup: all the data as an AES-256 ZIP file.

Records come in from CSV, JSON, Contacts or Tables, and files are attached from Files or Notes. A collection is shared at three levels, and the app can be read in 21 languages.

Good for

The cards, accounts and licences of a household or an office, shared with the people who need them.

Passwords and PINs that stay unreadable even to whoever runs the server.

FormulaBase — formulas you use again and again

FormulaBase is a calculator for the formulas you need over and over: mark-ups, unit conversions, loan payments, mixing ratios, engineering constants. Define a formula's variables once, with their labels, units and default values, then type in numbers and read the result as you type.

You do not start from a blank page: 5,522 built-in templates in thirteen fields, from geometry and statistics to electricity, money and health, are ready to drop into your own collections.

You see the mathematics, not just the answer:

  • A panel beside the result works the formula out one step at a time, and saves the steps to your Files as a spreadsheet or a document.
  • A formula marked “Reversible” is worked backwards: give it the result, and it finds the value.
  • Every formula keeps its history of calculations and of earlier versions.
  • More than 200 functions, running in your browser with no eval anywhere.

Good for

The calculations an office or a workshop repeats every day: prices with tax and mark-up, conversions, loan payments.

One shared set of formulas for a department, instead of everyone keeping their own.

NetBase — a network console

NetBase turns your Nextcloud into a network console. It finds every device on the local network, tells you what each one is, with its maker looked up from its address, and keeps the list: where each device stands and which ports it answers on. The list can be exported as CSV for an inventory.

Its device windows open each device's own settings page from inside Nextcloud, so a router, a switch, a printer or a NAS at a branch office can be looked after from anywhere the Nextcloud can be reached.

The everyday tools sit on the same screen:

  • DNS of every kind, and whois with a search for a free domain name;
  • TLS certificates, HTTP headers and redirects;
  • mail: SPF, DKIM and DMARC, a server test, and a real message sent and received;
  • FTP, SFTP and SSH with a real terminal, a clock check and speed tests.

What every tool finds can be saved into your Files. NetBase is an administrator's app, and each part can be opened to a chosen group.

Good for

Changing a branch router's settings without going there.

Working out why mail is not arriving, or why one office resolves a name differently from another.

Talk-Bot — AI chat in Nextcloud Talk

Talk-Bot turns any Nextcloud Talk conversation into a chat with an AI model. It runs as a Talk bot entirely inside Nextcloud, a few hundred kilobytes of PHP installed from the App Store, with no separate service to keep running. It answers off the request path, so posting a message never waits for the model.

Bring your own model: Claude and Gemini through their own APIs, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including a server of your own running Ollama. Or let a Claude or Gemini command-line subscription on the server answer everyone, with no API bill.

  • Two tiers: ordinary users get a chat and nothing else; administrators can be given tools to look after the server.
  • Memory per person and per conversation, and fair-use limits on questions.
  • Commands: ?help, ?reset, ?status, ?model and ?update.

Talk-Bot is being moved onto AI-Hub, the common AI interface of the series, so that its engine, its key and its limits are set once for every app on the server.

Good for

A helper in every team conversation, without sending anyone to another website.

A model on your own server, so the questions never leave it.

AI-Hub — one AI gateway for every app

AI-Hub is the common AI interface of the series. An app does not talk to a model: it registers a scenario — what the assistant is, which tools it may run and what shape its answers take — and then sends the user's words. AI-Hub chooses the engine, runs the conversation and the tools the scenario allows, checks the answer against the shape and hands it back, so the app can act on it.

The administrator sets up the engine once, for all apps: Claude and Gemini through their own APIs, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including a server of your own running Ollama, or a Claude or Gemini command-line subscription on the server. Every app that connects is listed, and can be given an AI and a model of its own.

  • Three ways in: from an app on the same server, over HTTP, and through Nextcloud's own Task Processing API, so Nextcloud Assistant and every app written against the standard API can use the connected model.
  • One place for who may ask, which apps may ask, questions per minute and answers in progress at once.
  • Safety: tools run with the rights of the person asking, through the app's own code; keys are stored encrypted and never leave the server.

Being adopted in turn. EditBase already asks AI-Hub for its assistant; Talk-Bot, RegiBase, FormulaBase and NetBase follow, so that one setting serves them all.

Open to every app. AI-Hub is not reserved for the apps on these pages: any Nextcloud app, by anyone, can register a scenario and ask, and an app that uses the standard Task Processing API needs no new code at all.

Good for

One AI setting, and one bill, for every app on the server.

An assistant that can act inside an app, because its answers come back in a shape the app checks.

All six apps are by KTEC and are published in the Nextcloud App Store. This document was laid out in EditBase.
